title.en: Economics: Employment in India and Tamil Nadu

text.en: Raju asked his uncle what he did for a living. "I work in a factory," he said.

Employment means working to earn a living. The economy has three sectors: the primary sector (farming, mining), the secondary sector (industry) and the tertiary sector (services). Workers may be in the organised sector with fixed pay and benefits or the unorganised sector without them.
Unemployment occurs when people who want work cannot find it. Types include disguised unemployment, where more people work on farms than needed, seasonal unemployment and educated unemployment.
Tamil Nadu has a strong industrial base and services sector, with textiles, automobiles and IT. Schemes such as MGNREGA guarantee 100 days of work in rural areas.
Employment means working to earn a living.
The economy has three sectors: the primary sector (farming, mining), the secondary sector (industry) and the tertiary sector (services).
Workers may be in the organised sector with fixed pay and benefits or the unorganised sector without them.
Unemployment occurs when people who want work cannot find it.
Types include disguised unemployment, where more people work on farms than needed, seasonal unemployment and educated unemployment.
Tamil Nadu has a strong industrial base and services sector, with textiles, automobiles and IT.
Schemes such as MGNREGA guarantee 100 days of work in rural areas.
To understand employment, we first look at the labour force: all people who are willing and able to work at the prevailing wage, whether they currently hold a job or are actively searching.
In India, the working-age population is generally counted from fifteen to fifty-nine years. Children in school and retired elders are outside the active workforce.
Let us compare the three economic sectors. Primary activities extract directly from nature: agriculture, forestry, fishing, dairy and mining.
Secondary activities transform raw materials into finished goods: cotton becomes yarn and shirts, iron ore becomes steel, and limestone becomes cement.
Tertiary activities provide services rather than physical goods: teachers, doctors, bus drivers, bank clerks, shopkeepers and software engineers all belong here.
Historically, most Indians worked in the primary sector. Over recent decades, the share of GDP from services and manufacturing has grown much faster than agriculture.
Now compare the organised and unorganised sectors. Organised workplaces are registered with the government and follow labour laws, fixed hours, paid leave and provident fund rules.
Examples of organised employers include government offices, public banks, large automobile factories and registered schools.
The unorganised sector includes street vendors, daily-wage farm labourers, small repair shops and home-based weavers. Jobs are often irregular and lack paid leave or pensions.
Because a huge majority of Indian workers are in the unorganised sector, social security schemes, minimum wage enforcement and skill training are vital.
We can also group employers into the public sector, owned by the government such as Indian Railways and BSNL, and the private sector, owned by individuals or companies.
Public enterprises aim to provide essential services at affordable rates, while private enterprises focus on innovation, competition and earning profit.
Let us examine types of unemployment carefully. Disguised unemployment happens when six people work on a small plot that really needs only three; removing three does not reduce output.

board.text: Disguised unemployment: extra hands, zero extra output

text.en: Seasonal unemployment occurs in farming and tourism when work is plentiful during sowing and harvest but scarce in off-season months.
Educated unemployment happens when graduates and diploma holders cannot find jobs matching their qualifications, often due to a gap between classroom theory and industry skills.
Tamil Nadu stands out among Indian states for high urbanisation and a diversified economy. Even rural households in Tamil Nadu earn a growing share from non-farm jobs.
Major industrial hubs include Chennai for automobiles and IT, Coimbatore for engineering and pumps, Tiruppur for knitwear exports, and Sivakasi for printing and matches.
Women's participation in Tamil Nadu's workforce is higher than the national average, supported by higher literacy, self-help groups and factory employment.

board.text: Higher female workforce participation in TN

text.en: To support rural livelihoods during lean agricultural months, the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act guarantees up to one hundred days of wage work per household each year.
MGNREGA projects build durable village assets such as desilted tanks, farm ponds and rural roads, while paying equal wages to women and men.
Vocational education, ITIs, apprenticeship programmes and startup support help young people move from low-wage casual labour into skilled, higher-paying careers.
When classifying any worker, ask two questions: which sector produces their output, and do they receive legal job security? That gives both their sector and organised status.
Healthy economic growth must create decent, safe and productive jobs across agriculture, manufacturing and services so every family benefits.

problem.en: A family of six works full-time on a one-hectare farm producing 30 bags of paddy. When two members take factory jobs in town, the remaining four still produce 30 bags. What type of unemployment was present?

text.en: Compare output before and after two workers leave.

why.en: Total paddy output stays at 30 bags even with four workers instead of six.

text.en: Identify the marginal contribution of the extra two workers.

why.en: Their extra labour added zero additional output to the harvest.

text.en: Name the unemployment type.

why.en: This is disguised unemployment: workers appeared busy, yet the farm did not need their labour.
